clue.text: Man maybe taken in by crazy fool

indicators.note: to be taken in by something is to be absorbed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: crazy means mad
the Isle of Man is one example of an isle, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: A man of some sort is fooled by a madcap joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, and 'maybe' flags it as one example of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone is to deceive or trick them, which is one verb sense of fool.

clue.text: Writing about a boring plant with familiar blooms

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer piece goes round what follows

blocks.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
taken as written
an oil rig is a plant that bores into the sea bed
familiar as in an old friend or an old story

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a dull plant that comes with well-known flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring plant' reads as a dull flower, but the plant is industrial machinery that drills for oil, and 'familiar' is used as in an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigolds are common orange and yellow garden flowers, so they are examples of blooms.

clue.text: Perhaps Miss Piggy assumes auditorium is empty

indicators.note: to assume is to take on or take in, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: Miss Piggy of the Muppets is a female pig, a sow
a concert hall is an auditorium

explanation.surface: The Muppet diva takes it for granted that the theatre has no audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Miss Piggy, the Muppet, as an example of a female pig rather than a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow is used of talk or people lacking depth or substance, which is a figurative sense of empty.

clue.text: Age of ambassador holding policewoman back

indicators.note: holding means gripping inside, so one piece contains the other
going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a cop is a police officer of either sex

explanation.surface: An ambassador of a certain age restrains a policewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, for His Excellency, is the standard crossword abbreviation for an ambassador; a cop can be a policewoman as readily as a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long, distinct period of history, so it is a synonym of age in that sense.

clue.text: Dehydrated? Doctor has seconds to give her advice

indicators.note: seconds here are the second letters of each of the following words

blocks.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
the second letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A patient is dehydrated, and the doctor takes a moment to advise her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like a moment of time, but it picks out the second letter of each word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dried has had its water removed, which is exactly what dehydrated describes.

clue.text: Accept honour after cycling competition

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so a letter from one end of the word comes round to the other end

blocks.note: an MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: Someone takes an award after a bike race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling competition' reads as a bike race, but cycling acts on the honour: its last letter rotates to the front. The MBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or offer is to welcome and adopt it willingly, a figurative synonym of accept.

clue.text: New girder a civil engineer used for support tunnels, reported writer

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so these letters are reformed into a different order
a report is something said, so the word is given by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer
burrows are animal tunnels

explanation.surface: A new girder is put in by an engineer to shore up some tunnels, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used for support' only bridges the anagram to the tunnels, and the closing 'writer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs was the American novelist who created Tarzan and John Carter of Mars.

clue.text: See 5
Celebrate Viagra's latest cracking blue tablet

indicators.note: the latest of anything is its final item, so only the end letter is kept
to crack something is to break into it, so one piece lodges inside the other

blocks.note: blue as in a blue movie, an adult one
the final letter of the drug's name
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A man celebrates the newest little blue pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue tablet' looks like Viagra itself, but blue means risqué, and the tablet is E for ecstasy. The A breaks into ADULT before the E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to praise or admire someone excessively, so it means celebrating them lavishly.

clue.text: Put up before court

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone is brought up in front of a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up before court' sounds like standing trial, but 'Put up' is the definition and the rest builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a building or tent is to construct or raise it, which is to put it up.

clue.text: Thinking about a shanty for one without home

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a sea shanty is one example of a song
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A homeless person muses about a sea shanty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without home' reads as homeless, but 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps another.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the process of working something out logically, so it is a synonym for thinking.

clue.text: Dictator's radical course

indicators.note: a dictator is one who dictates, speaking words out for someone to write down

blocks.note: radical comes from the Latin for root, and a radical in maths is a root

explanation.surface: A tyrant's extreme policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a tyrant, but here it is someone dictating, saying words for another to take down; in British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is the way or path taken to reach somewhere, which is a sense of course.

clue.text: Noble sort of festivity enjoyed

blocks.note: a gala is a festive occasion
to have had a good time is to have enjoyed it

explanation.surface: An aristocratic kind of party went down well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble sort of festivity' looks like a grand party, but 'Noble sort' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad of Arthurian legend stands for a pure, chivalrous man, so a galahad is a noble type.

clue.text: Sussex town besieged, we hear – it may be read as a warning

definitions.text: it may be read as a warning

indicators.note: what we hear is what is spoken, so the answer is given by sound

blocks.note: Rye is a small town in East Sussex, and besieged means attacked

explanation.surface: A south-coast town under siege gets a formal warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is an old harbour town in East Sussex, on England's south coast. The definition alludes to the phrase 'read the riot act', meaning give a stern telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was a British law read aloud to order crowds to disperse; reading it now means scolding someone.

clue.text: In America, game wife dancing in ballgown holds in ...

indicators.note: to hold is to keep inside, so the outer letters take in the others
dancing letters move about and change places with one another

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written
the second in, taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife dancing in her ballgown is game for something, the dots promising more.
explanation.walkthrough: The wife and the final 'in' all go into the shuffle with BALLGOWN; the dots lead on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn bowling is the usual North American name for bowls, played by rolling biased balls toward a jack on grass.

clue.text: Ordered pawnbroker to get her ring out – ultimately you should be 16

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a new sequence
something out is taken away, so these letters are dropped from the mix
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
a ring is round like the letter O
the last letter of you

explanation.surface: A customer tells a pawnbroker to fetch her ring out of hock.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one O out of the pawnbroker phrase, add the U, and rearrange. 16 refers to the answer at 16-across, to err.
explanation.definitionFit: To bark up the wrong tree is an idiom for pursuing a mistaken idea, which is to err.

clue.text: See 14
... boob, somewhat overreacting

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only a part of the next word is used

blocks.note: found in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a blunder made by somebody who rather overreacts.
explanation.walkthrough: Boob is British slang for a blunder, used here as a verb meaning to make a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, and to boob is informal British slang for exactly that.

clue.text: North Yorkshire town, favourite place to see stars

blocks.note: Redcar is a seaside town on the North Yorkshire coast
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A northern town is the best spot for stargazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See stars' suggests astronomy, but these stars are celebrities. Redcar is a seaside town in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Film premieres roll out a red carpet for celebrities to walk along, so it is where famous people appear.

clue.text: Second, very big distress signal

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
OS stands for outsize, the clothing size label

explanation.surface: A second huge cry for help.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing label for outsize, meaning extra large.
explanation.definitionFit: SOS is the international Morse code call for help used by ships and aircraft in trouble.

clue.text: Promise that's been broken, like many in the lower leagues

definitions.text: like many in the lower leagues

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, which can be put back together in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken promise, of the kind common among footballers in the lower divisions.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym, so it must be read as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Players in lower football leagues are often paid part-time while holding other jobs, making them semi-professional.

clue.text: Correct sir, he, Donald Trump is president here

indicators.note: to correct something is to fix it, rearranging what was wrong into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone addresses Donald Trump, noting where he is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donald Trump' reads as one name, but Donald joins the letters while Trump starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhode Island is one of the American states, all of which come under the US president's authority.

clue.text: For example Nelson Mandela regularly turned on awful liar

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so letters are taken at a fixed spacing
something turned faces the other way, so the letters run in reverse
awful means a mess, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: every third letter, starting with the first
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nelson Mandela is accused of turning on a dreadful liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nelson Mandela' looks like one name, but Nelson belongs to the definition and Mandela to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson, victor at Trafalgar, was a British admiral, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Hot food rejected by order – on your head be it!

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run the other way

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A diner sends back hot food, telling the waiter the blame lies with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your head be it' is an idiom meaning you take the blame, but here it is literal: something you wear on your head.
explanation.definitionFit: A homburg is a felt hat with a dented crown and curled brim, so it is worn on the head.

clue.text: After greeting King, journalist rambled

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Having greeted the King, a reporter waffled on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambled' suggests talking at length, but here it means walking in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use, to ramble is to go on a leisurely country walk, much the same as going on a hike.

clue.text: Spinning top with novel problem

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: a lid is the top of a container
Emma is the novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A spinning top poses a fresh puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning top' reads as a child's toy, and 'novel problem' as a new difficulty; top is a lid and the novel is Austen's.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult situation requiring a choice between unwelcome options, so it is a kind of problem.

clue.text: Dopes in essentially dodgy toupees

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter, the third of the five in the word
rug is slang for a toupee

explanation.surface: Idiots in dubious hairpieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dopes' reads as fools, but it is a verb: to sedate with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dope a person or racehorse is to give them a sedative or stimulant, which is to drug them.

clue.text: Case to explain after youth is charged

indicators.note: a case is the outside shell of something, so only the outer letters are kept
after places the first-named piece behind the second-named one in the answer

blocks.note: a lad is a young man
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A young man is charged and must explain himself in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'charged' suggest a court case, but charged means loaded, and case means the outside of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or burdened, and charged can mean filled or loaded, as in a charged glass.

clue.text: Broken Ford next to drive

blocks.note: the Ka is a small Ford car
to put or drive is to push or thrust something somewhere, as in putting a shot

explanation.surface: A broken-down car beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ka was a small hatchback sold by Ford in Britain and Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is an informal word, borrowed from German, for something that no longer works.

clue.text: Return trigger after bullet

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second-named one in the answer

blocks.note: a round is a single bullet or cartridge
to trip a switch is to trigger it

explanation.surface: A gunman squeezes the trigger again after firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' sounds like firing back, but it is a ticket covering both directions of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A return in Britain is a ticket there and back, which Americans call a round trip.

clue.text: See terms of the government's green papers in recess

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the end letter of each word is kept
a recess is a withdrawal or retreat, so the letters back away and run the other way

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the final letter, ignoring the apostrophe
eco- is the prefix meaning environmentally friendly, or green
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Look at what the government's green papers say while Parliament is in recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction, but it is the definition. Green papers are British government consultation documents, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's area of authority, and that territory is also called a diocese.

clue.text: Top one percent finally

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter is used

blocks.note: single means one
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: The richest one percent, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top one percent' reads as the wealthy elite, but 'Top' is a garment. A singlet is the British word for a vest or tank top.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless undershirt or athletic vest, which is a kind of top worn on the upper body.
